svg.text: Each driver loads on the one below and the application only sees the COM name, so a fault in any layer looks like a COM port problem.

svg.text: VID 0403 = FTDI · 067B = Prolific · 10C4 = Silicon Labs · 1A86 = WCH (CH340)

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Clone Prolific or FTDI chips: current drivers refuse them (Code 10).

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Rolling back is a workaround at best; the fix is a genuine adapter.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: a chip with no serial number is identified by its USB socket, so moving it creates a new device and a new COMn;

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the old device keeps its ComDB reservation as a hidden ghost (Code 45). Label the socket, or use an adapter with a unique serial.
